summary: Chunks of yam simmered in a tomato, pepper and palm oil sauce until they soften and thicken the pot into a hearty porridge.
story: Yam porridge, called asaro in Yoruba, is a comforting one-pot meal of yam cooked down in a spiced pepper sauce. It is a popular family dinner, and cooks often add fish, smoked turkey or leafy greens.

steps.title: Prepare the yam
steps.text: Peel the yam, cut into cubes and rinse in cold water to remove excess starch. Drain well. Soak in lightly salted water if you cannot cook straight away.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, scotch bonnet and the blending half of the onion until fairly smooth.

steps.title: Heat the palm oil
steps.text: Heat the palm oil in a medium pot over medium heat for about 2 minutes until it is hot and smells fragrant but is not smoking. Fry the chopped onion for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Fry the sauce
steps.text: Add the blended mixture and fry for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until the sauce has darkened and thickened and oil rises to the top.

steps.title: Add yam and liquid
steps.text: Stir in the crayfish, cubes and fish. Add the yam and just enough water to nearly cover. Season with salt.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low for 15 to 20 minutes until the yam pieces are fork tender. Mash a few pieces against the side of the pot with a spoon to thicken the porridge naturally.

steps.title: Add greens
steps.text: Stir in the greens, if using, and cook for 2 minutes until just wilted. Taste, adjust salt and serve hot.

tips: Do not stir too often or the yam will break down before it is cooked.
Add the water gradually. You want a thick porridge, not a soup.
Cooked greens added at the end keep their colour.
Use firm, white yam for the best texture.

swaps.swap: Use sweet potato for a sweeter, softer porridge or firm potatoes in a pinch. Cooking time will be shorter.
Vegetable oil with a little paprika gives colour but not the same flavour.
Spinach or kale make easy substitutes.

name: Yam Porridge (Asaro)
